interpretation.plain_speak: Changing which new examples come last still helped learn this second vocabulary family, but it did not improve old-vocabulary memory because old retention was already equally high in every arm. The earlier retention benefit therefore is not a universal rule across lexical families.
interpretation.north_star_question: Tests whether a scheduling mechanism for sequential lexical learning generalizes across disjoint language families without extra memory or training budget.
interpretation.next_stage: run a paired same-harness family-by-diversity interaction test to distinguish a family-dependent retention effect from run-to-run or implementation differences
